verdicts.correction: The core is confirmed. I re-ran the calls on 2026-10-24 with no cookie. The 403 says 'XSRF token invalid' and returns an x-csrf-token header (value 9BPntHEa3vgM, the same value as the researcher's capture). Server returns 401 as a bare JSON string, and 'server' or 6 maps to 'Server'. The x-ratelimit-limit header is 10000, 10000;w=60. Unknown types return 404 'unhandled link type'. Three parts are wrong: (1) 'Every game-relevant type needs a cookie' is false. ExperienceAffiliate maps to a Place in L6 and resolves with 200 without a cookie, and ShareLinks.js deliberately resolves ExperienceAffiliate and AvatarItemAffiliate for guests. (2) 'Value 12 is unnamed' is wrong. The server accepts the name 'AvatarItemAffiliate' in any case, and it returns 200 with avatarItemDetailsData {status:'Invalid', itemId:null, itemType:null}, identical to 12. (3) Out-of-range numbers are not rejected: linkType 13 returns 401 "User must be authenticated to use '13' links". Also, a body with no linkType returns 500 {"Error":"unknown exception"}, not 400.

privateServerInviteData does carry placeId, ownerUserId and privateServerId. linkCode is a JSON string. The full shape is {status:'Invalid'|'Valid'|'Expired', ownerUserId:number, universeId:number, privateServerId:number, linkCode:string, placeId:number}. Three sources support this. RoSeal's type PrivateServerLinkData (last commit 2026-08-26) has these fields, and its PrivateServerLink.tsx reads inviteData.linkCode and inviteData.ownerUserId. The openblox wrapper has a captured example (2024-10): {"status":"Valid","ownerUserId":45348281,"universeId":6430220996,"privateServerId":1630945839,"linkCode":"67771413747491684286858666824242","placeId":18980972074}. Froststrap's GameJoin.cs (2026-10-18) reads data.placeId with TryGetInt64 and linkCode with GetString, then launches roblox://experiences/start?placeId=..&linkCode=.. In the example, placeId equals the universe's rootPlaceId: games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=6430220996 returns rootPlaceId 18980972074. What is still true: Roblox's own web code (CoreUtilities.js, verified) reads only status, universeId and linkCode, and maps universeId to rootPlaceId. The pealz1 regex for "placeId" is therefore not broken. RoALT can use placeId directly and fall back to the universeId lookup.

I re-verified the flow. /share returns 302 to ro.blox.com/Ebh5 with af_dp, deep_link_value and af_web_dp. ShareLinks.js gates resolution on isAuthenticated, ExperienceAffiliate or AvatarItemAffiliate. CoreUtilities' SW calls joinPrivateGame(placeId, null, linkCode). GameLaunch.js builds {placeId, accessCode:null, linkCode}, which jQuery.param serialises as accessCode= with request=RequestPrivateGame. One part is overstated: that scraping joinPrivateGame from the page is 'dead'. I also saw 0 matches, but only on a guest fetch, where data-private-server-link-code stays empty even with ?privateServerLinkCode in the URL. Maintained tools still scrape it from the logged-in game page to get the GUID accessCode: RoSeal's getPrivateServerStatusByCode, matching /joinPrivateGame\(\d+?, '(.+?)', '.+?'\)/ (RoSeal repo active 2026-10-23), and niccsprojects/Roblox-Account-Manager's private_links.rs (Tauri/Rust, 2026-07-15). ethanstoner #14 only says the code 'may no longer be there' and is tagged needs-account-test. Whether the logged-in page still has it is unknown, so do not depend on it either way.

The claim is correctly hedged. The web code has no accept step between resolve and /games/{root}?privateServerLinkCode=. The staff quote is confirmed: on 2023-10-02 spottedriverturtle wrote 'Roblox is still using the Private Server Link Code and Game ID under the hood' and 'All pre-existing links will continue to work.' Two additions. (1) The web still has a private-server privacy page: CoreUtilities route private_server_subsettings maps to /my/account#!/privacy/VisibilityAndPrivateServers/PrivateServerPrivacy. The API key name is still unconfirmed, and apis.roblox.com/user-settings-api/v1/user-settings returns 401 9002 without a cookie. (2) Issue #11 lists user-settings-api explicitly only as the follow-privacy replacement; for private-server-invite-privacy it says only 'same API'. Weak community evidence (a FRAM author, 2026-04) says that converting a share link to /games/..?privateServerLinkCode= and then joining works across alts. Cross-account join without resolve is still untested.

I re-captured /share?code=abc123&v=v2: it returns 302 with pid=sharelinkv2 and af_force_deeplink=true, and has no deep_link_value. POST apis.roblox.com/deeplinks/v2/resolve returns 403 XSRF, then 401 {errors:[{code:9002,...'Authentication token is missing'}]}. The web code compares data.linkType to 'Experience', 'StudioEdit', 'StudioTeamTest', 'UserTrustedConnection', 'StudioTrustedConnection', Moments and Referral. The Referral path goes to Roblox Plus as referralCode. ShareLinks.js treats v case-insensitively (o.toLowerCase()==='v2'). RoSeal shows the creation side: v2 create takes {linkType:'Experience'|'StudioEdit'|'StudioTeamTest', targetId, customData:object} and returns {link}. v2 and ExperienceAffiliate links can expire. The Share Link API (SocialService:PromptLinkSharing, DevForum 2025-10-02) has ExpirationSeconds defaulting to 86400 and a FallbackLinkId.

I verified the handlers in CoreUtilities.js. Some nuances. For experienceDetailsInviteData the web acts only on status Valid, and it only navigates to /games/{rootPlaceId}?shareLinkSourceType=ExperienceDetails without auto-launching. avatarItemDetailsData also has status (seen live). friendInviteData also has status (Valid|Expired|Consumed|SenderBlockedRecipient|Invalid) and friendingToken (RoSeal). experienceInviteData may include launchData (RoSeal type). For a valid instance invite the web calls SW(placeId, placeId, instanceId, ..., inviterId), which goes to joinGameInstance (RequestGameJob). For notification and screenshot invites the web double-encodes launchData: encodeURIComponent(encodeURIComponent(x)). ExperienceAffiliate with Valid and no universeId falls back to /users/{fallbackId}/profile or a referral home page.

Confirmed. pyrobloxbot shows the share code 864059867507234896ed98bd1b78a8dc resolving to /games/90906407195271/Racket-Rivals?privateServerLinkCode=1020499390872690887970171 (25 digits). It also says 'If the private server's invite link gets regenerated, then the private server link code will also change.' RoSeal uses /^\d+$/ for privateServerLinkCode and linkCode. The DevForum thread is dated 2025-02-11 (solution 2025-02-19) with code ce65b2c8..., 32 hex. More 2026 samples are 32-digit (ReTwisted #15, FRAM #1), and so is the openblox resolve response. Caution: some tools hard-code exactly 32 digits (ReTwisted uses [0-9]{32}). RoALT must not.

Every redirect and status reproduced exactly on 2026-10-24: 301 slug canonicalisation keeping the query, apex 308, web 302 to www:443, m.roblox.com 404 (root too), /de 200, /pt-br to /pt, /zh-cn to no prefix, /GAMES 200, /games/0 to request-error, /experiences 404, and /share 10 per 60 s. More observations: /en-us/games/... returns 302 to the unprefixed path. /games/{id} has a rate limit of 100 per 60 s. Legacy /PlaceItem.aspx?id=920587237 returns 301 to /games/920587237/view. /places/{id} returns 404. RoSeal's LOCALE_REGEX is /^[a-z]{2}(-[a-z0-9]{2,3})?$/i, and the 'js'/'my' exclusion is in DeepLinkParser.ts, not in constants.ts.

Confirmed. The deep-linking page says 'This process is deprecated' and points to share links. It documents the 200-byte decoded launchData limit and the 'Followed user has left the game' error. The guest /games/start inline script still emits only roblox://experiences/start?placeId=920587237&launchData=abc and drops gameInstanceId (re-captured).

Confirmed: the constants ExperienceLauncher 'roblox://experiences/start?' and AppLauncher 'roblox://navigation', the Sm precedence (linkCode, then accessCode, then launchData, then joinMultiplayerGame), Bloxstrap GetInviteDeeplink, and the BTRoblox README param list. Three nuances in the web's own parser (Sw): it uses regexes /\/(\w+)/g and /(\w+)=([^&=]+)/g over the whole URL, so keys are case-sensitive, values are not URL-decoded, and empty values are not captured. The legacy placeId handler (Sm) ignores gameInstanceId. Case-insensitive key matching is RoSeal's behaviour, not Roblox's.

Confirmed in RoSeal's DeepLinkParser.ts. It checks that the URL starts with https://ro.blox.com/Ebh5, reads af_dp first and falls back to deep_link_value ('prioritize mobile over web'), and uses af_web_dp last. Roblox's docs page describes ro.blox.com/Ebh5?af_dp=..&af_web_dp=.. as an AppsFlyer link.

Re-captured: servers/Public returns 200 with x-ratelimit-limit 3, 3;w=60. Item keys are fps, id, maxPlayers, ping, playerTokens, players and playing. IDs are lowercase GUIDs with version nibble 4, for example 54d0ed42-1ad3-4143-88fd-56b59595df5c. The presence swagger types gameId as format uuid. The pyrobloxbot underscore example is not a GUID. The parser should accept any GUID and not enforce version 4.

Confirmed: GameLaunch.js followPlayerIntoGame uses placelauncherurl request=RequestFollowUser. The presence POST works without a cookie or CSRF token and has a rate limit of 60 per 60 s. The swagger PresenceType enum is [0,1,2,3] and gameId is a uuid. Not independently confirmable: that another user's 'who can join me' setting cannot be read (the only source is a 2023 DevForum thread), the option names, and the user-settings key. Leave this as medium or uncertain until an authenticated test.

Confirmed from the docs: GET games.roblox.com/v1/games/{placeId}/private-servers is EXPERIMENTAL and its fields include vipServerId, accessCode and owner, plus gameJoinRestricted. Without a cookie it returns 401 9002. PATCH /v1/vip-servers/{id} returns joinCode and link. can-invite returns {canInvite, doesOwnerPrivacyRestrictJoins, inviteResponseType}. An accessCode can also come from scraping the logged-in game page (RoSeal and nicc RAM, see L3), from Bloxstrap activity data, or from the list endpoint above.

Mostly right, with small errors. friends, accountsettings and presence /docs/json/v1 return 302 to prod.docsiteassets.roblox.com/assets/en-us/cloud/legacy/<svc>/v1.json. games.roblox.com/docs/json/v1 and v2 return 404 and do NOT redirect, although the docsiteassets file .../legacy/games/v1.json exists (200). It has 8 paths (9 operations), not 9 paths. gamejoin's docsiteassets copy returns 403, and gamejoin.roblox.com/docs/json/v1 returns 404. apis.roblox.com/sharelinks/docs/json/v1 returns 404.

I re-ran ref_parse.py against links-parse-cases.json: 38/38 pass. Adversarial inputs found gaps to fix before porting. (1) An empty value (accessCode=, gameInstanceId=, privateServerLinkCode=) returns Invalid. The web treats empty as absent, because Sw's regex needs [^&=]+ and Sm uses truthiness. Ignore empty values. (2) parse_qsl decodes '+' as a space, so launchData 'a+b' becomes 'a b'. Roblox's own parser does no decoding, and Rust's form_urlencoded does the same as parse_qsl. Decide this explicitly and add a test. (3) Hosts parse differently: Python urlsplit reads 'https://evil.com\@www.roblox.com/games/1' as host www.roblox.com, while WHATWG parsers such as the Rust url crate read evil.com. Fixture results will diverge, so add the case. (4) The legacy /PlaceItem.aspx?id=N redirects to /games/N/view and should give Place. It currently gives Unsupported. (5) /games/{id}?linkCode=.. silently drops the code and gives Place. Consider a warning. (6) The RoSeal static form roblox://navigation/share_links/{type}/{code} gives Unsupported. (7) A bare number is always read as Place, which is ambiguous with user IDs; show this in the UI.

missed.claim: The real private-server resolve payload includes placeId, ownerUserId and privateServerId, and linkCode is a string.
missed.detail: The shape is privateServerInviteData = {status, ownerUserId, universeId, privateServerId, linkCode:string, placeId}. Example: {"status":"Valid","ownerUserId":45348281,"universeId":6430220996,"privateServerId":1630945839,"linkCode":"67771413747491684286858666824242","placeId":18980972074}. Here placeId equals rootPlaceId. Froststrap (2026-10-18) relies on placeId and linkCode. RoALT can skip the universe-to-root lookup when placeId is present.

missed.claim: Share-link creation endpoints exist and are useful for a 'copy invite link' feature.
missed.detail: POST https://apis.roblox.com/sharelinks/v1/create-link and /sharelinks/v1/get-or-create-link take {linkType, data: JSON.stringify(...)}. They return {deepLinkUrl, linkId, shortUrl}. The data for ScreenshotInvite is {placeId, instanceId?, launchData?}, for ExperienceDetails {universeId}, and for AvatarItemDetails {itemType, itemId}. v2 creation is {linkType:'Experience'|'StudioEdit'|'StudioTeamTest', targetId, customData} and returns {link}. All of these use cookie credentials. This comes from RoSeal source and was not verified live.

missed.claim: Active 2026 tools still get the GUID accessCode by scraping the logged-in game page, so 'scraping is dead' is not established.
missed.detail: RoSeal's getPrivateServerStatusByCode fetches /games/{placeId}/{name}?privateServerLinkCode=.. with cookies, finds the script containing joinPrivateGame, and matches /joinPrivateGame\(\d+?, '(.+?)', '.+?'\)/. niccsprojects/Roblox-Account-Manager, a Tauri/Rust app (2026-07-15), does the same with fallbacks for "accessCode":" markers. Guest captures show data-private-server-link-code="", so only an authenticated fetch can settle this. Prefer the linkCode path, which the current web uses with accessCode empty.

missed.claim: Passing roblox://placeId=..&linkCode=.. straight to the desktop client is unreliable. The web never does this.
missed.detail: The web's legacy handler (Sm) turns linkCode deep links into the web page /games/{id}?privateServerLinkCode= and joins through PlaceLauncher RequestPrivateGame. ReTwisted launches roblox://placeId={id}&linkCode={code} directly, and its 2026 issues report landing in an empty public server (#13, 2026-03-23; #15, 2026-06-13). This is community evidence and the cause is unconfirmed. It supports RoALT using the placelauncherurl RequestPrivateGame&placeId&accessCode=&linkCode= rather than deep links.

missed.claim: Creator share links and the in-experience Share Link API produce links that can expire, and creator ones carry LaunchData.
missed.detail: The Creator Dashboard (Creations > Share Links) builds links with optional custom LaunchData and no per-game limit (create.roblox.com/docs/production/promotion/share-links). SocialService:PromptLinkSharing was announced on 2025-10-02 by the Moments Product Lead. It has LinkSharingOptions LaunchData, PreviewTitle, PreviewDescription, ExpirationSeconds (default 86400) and FallbackLinkId. Expired links should therefore be expected, as Expired status or a fallback. These are the likely sources of type=ExperienceAffiliate, v=v2 and Moments links in the wild.

missed.claim: The server-side resolve-link enum includes AvatarItemAffiliate. The error shapes vary.
missed.detail: linkType 'AvatarItemAffiliate' (any case, or 12) returns 200 without a cookie. Out-of-range 13 returns 401 "User must be authenticated to use '13' links". A missing linkType returns 500 {"Error":"unknown exception"}. A missing linkId returns 400 "Error while resolving the link." The error handler must accept a bare string, the {errors:[]} envelope, and the {Error:..} object.

missed.claim: The legacy /PlaceItem.aspx?id= URL shape still redirects and is missing from the parser.
missed.detail: GET https://www.roblox.com/PlaceItem.aspx?id=920587237 returns 301 to /games/920587237/view. /places/{id} returns 404 and /en-us/games/.. returns 302 to the unprefixed path. Add /PlaceItem.aspx?id=N → Place{N} to R4 and the test cases.

missed.claim: The web double-encodes launchData in the roblox://experiences/start links it builds.
missed.detail: For NotificationExperienceInvite and ScreenshotInvite, CoreUtilities builds '&launchData='+encodeURIComponent(encodeURIComponent(launchData)). A pasted deep link from that path decodes to a still-percent-encoded string after one pass. The legacy Sm handler passes launchData through without decoding. Define one decode policy and test it against the 200-byte limit, which applies to the decoded value.

missed.claim: The private-server privacy setting still exists on the web.
missed.detail: CoreUtilities routes private_server_subsettings to /my/account#!/privacy/VisibilityAndPrivateServers/PrivateServerPrivacy. The setting lives under 'Visibility and Private Servers', and its API key in user-settings-api is still unknown. GameLaunch.js reads apis.roblox.com/user-settings-api/v1/user-settings/settings-and-options, where contentAgeRestriction was observed. That endpoint is the likely place to discover the key names with an authenticated call.
